stem: According to the first law of thermodynamics, when heat is added to a system, what are the two possible outcomes?

options.A: It decreases the internal energy and no work is done.
options.B: It increases the internal energy and work is done on the environment.
options.C: It decreases the internal energy and work is done by the environment.
options.D: It increases the internal energy and no work is done.

solution_latex: The first law of thermodynamics states that $\\Delta U = Q - W$, where $\\Delta U$ is the change in internal energy, $Q$ is the heat added to the system, and $W$ is the work done by the system. If heat is added to the system ($Q > 0$), the internal energy can increase ($\\\\Delta U > 0$) and/or work can be done by the system ($W > 0$). Therefore, when heat is added to a system, it increases the internal energy of the system plus work is done on the environment.
